**Anthropic's production research system is the same orchestrator-worker shape, with explicit effort-scaling rules and checkpointed resume.** The lead agent spawns 3-5 subagents in parallel, each with an objective, an output format, tool guidance and task boundaries; effort is scaled by query complexity (simple fact-finding: 1 agent, 3-10 tool calls; direct comparison: 2-4 subagents, 10-15 calls each; complex research: more than 10 subagents). It reports multi-agent runs at about 15× the tokens of a chat, and names synchronous subagent execution as a bottleneck. The concrete transfer: add an effort-scaling table to `research.md` and `review.md` (simple / comparison / complex → lineages × iterations × tool calls), which this runtime lacks; its floors are per-kind, not per-complexity. Value: an operator sizes a run without arithmetic. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system]

**LangChain's Open Deep Research exposes per-researcher limits and a published cost table.** Its supervisor-researcher graph caps researcher iterations, runs researchers in parallel, and its README reports total cost and tokens per benchmark run ($45.98 / 58.0M tokens for the default, $187.09 / 138.9M for Claude Sonnet 4). The concrete transfer: put a `budget` block on each lineage (`maxIterations`, `maxToolCalls`, estimated cost) and print it before spawn, so the operator sees the price the way LangChain's table shows it. Value: makes cost a first-class parameter instead of a post-hoc surprise. Effort S/M. Risk low. [SOURCE: https://github.com/langchain-ai/open_deep_research]

**Tree of Thoughts makes search explicit: generate candidates, self-evaluate, then expand or backtrack.** ToT's contribution is deliberate search over coherent thoughts with evaluation and backtracking, not a fixed left-to-right chain. This runtime's frontier grows by structural admission only (relevance, dedupe, depth, fan-out, budget, cycle) and its focus order is shallowest → least visited → oldest; neither step scores expected value. The concrete transfer: add an optional `priority` (or `expectedValue`) field to `frontier_proposal` and rank focus by it after depth, so a high-value child is not queued behind an older low-value one. Value: growth follows value, not arrival order. Effort M. Risk medium (a model-authored priority must not be trusted over the caps). [SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10601]

**STORM gets breadth from distinct perspectives, not from more questions in one voice.** STORM discovers diverse perspectives and simulates writers who pose questions from each, then curates an outline; its evaluation attributes coverage gains to that multi-perspective asking. This runtime's seed asks for 3-6 sub-questions that "together cover the topic", with no perspective requirement and a text-based dedupe key. The concrete transfer: require each seed question to name a distinct perspective or role and dedupe on that perspective, which also gives the proposal admission a semantic axis that plain text comparison lacks. Value: less near-duplicate seeding, broader first-pass coverage. Effort S. Risk low. [SOURCE: https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.14207]
